responseText: {"title":"Room to Breathe","question":"What does the space around a figure do to it?","introduction":"Eight works place figures — human, animal, skeletal, coiled — inside fields that dwarf, dissolve, or press against them. Some figures dissolve at their edges; others hold a hard silhouette against emptiness. Moving through the gallery, notice how the surrounding ground is never neutral: it crowds, radiates, glows, or simply waits.","closing":"Each work leaves a different amount of room. Whether that room reads as freedom, exposure, or pressure may depend on what the figure itself is doing with its edges.","chapters":[{"title":"Edges That Give Way","introduction":"Two works open the exhibition by showing figures whose outlines are actively undone — one by layered washes, one by a field of organic forms pressing inward from every side.","stops":[{"slot":"W003","whyHere":"The hat brim and face dissolve into overlapping pale circles; figure and background trade places across the surface, making the boundary itself the subject.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W020","whyHere":"Rounded forms crowd in from all edges while the pale center holds open; like W003, the figure-ground boundary is unstable, but here pressure comes from outside rather than within.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W003 dissolves outward through soft circles, W020 reverses the direction — dense forms push inward, leaving only a lit center to resist them."}]},{"title":"Silhouette and the Open Field","introduction":"Three works strip the figure to a flat black shape and set it against a single saturated ground, testing how much a solid form can hold when surrounded by open color.","stops":[{"slot":"W106","whyHere":"A black animal silhouette occupies the lower-right corner of a vast blue field; yellow zigzag marks radiate outward, the only evidence of energy in an otherwise empty expanse.","transitionFromPrevious":"After W020's crowded edges, the sky-blue field of W106 empties almost entirely — the figure shrinks to a corner, and the surrounding space becomes the dominant presence."},{"slot":"W220","whyHere":"A small black figure raises one arm in a yellow field that fills the entire canvas; wavy lines fan from its head, but the yellow above remains unbroken and vast.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works use a flat black silhouette against a single-color ground, but W220 centers its figure lower and surrounds it with even more uninterrupted field above."},{"slot":"W265","whyHere":"A coiled black form rests on a black ground strip; lines burst outward into yellow, yet the large empty upper field makes the stillness feel heavier than the radiating marks suggest.","transitionFromPrevious":"W220's figure reaches upward into open yellow; W265's coiled form turns inward, its shell enclosing a spiral while the same yellow field above reads as weight rather than openness."}]},{"title":"Figure Holding Its Ground","introduction":"Two works show figures that occupy more of the picture plane — one gripping an object across open space, one contained within a dark inner frame — where the surrounding field becomes a threshold rather than an absence.","stops":[{"slot":"W237","whyHere":"A standing figure grips a tangle of lines stretching to a glowing disc; soft color washes keep the ground open, but the figure's reach claims the horizontal space around it.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W265's form is closed and still, W237's figure extends an arm across the composition, actively measuring the space it stands in."},{"slot":"W250","whyHere":"A hunched figure sits inside a dark inner rectangle while soft light circles drift across the warm outer field; the framed boundary makes the surrounding space feel like a separate zone.","transitionFromPrevious":"W237's figure stands in open, undivided space; W250 introduces a literal frame within the image, splitting the field into an inner pressure and an outer glow."}]},{"title":"Close and Contained","introduction":"The final work brings a figure forward into near-total darkness, where the surrounding field offers almost nothing — making the figure's own surface the only available space.","stops":[{"slot":"W258","whyHere":"A compact skeletal figure stands against deep black; white and orange lines trace its limbs from within, so the figure carries its own light rather than drawing it from any surrounding field.","transitionFromPrevious":"W250's figure is held inside a dark rectangle with a glowing field beyond; W258 removes that outer glow entirely, leaving the figure alone in black with only its own traced edges as light."}]}]}
